research_priority.theme: Quality ex-AI cash-flow beneficiaries of breadth broadening without small-cap balance-sheet risk
research_priority.rationale: The relevant swing factor is the regime’s explicit breadth conflict: equal weight is still lagging cap weight, with RSP up 11.9% over 3M versus SPY up 14.8%, but the internal breadth measures are improving — 81.8% of stocks are above their 200-day moving average, ADL slope is +0.62, and IWM has led SPY by 5.8 percentage points over 3M. That makes a broadening-away-from-AI thesis plausible, but not clean enough to simply buy all beta. Credit is supportive, with the credit layer bullish at 8.3 and HY OAS tight around 276bps, which helps non-AI cyclicals and quality cash-flow compounders participate. The constraint is that sticky AI leadership remains a near-equal regime runner-up, with Reopening / Soft Landing at 36.2% versus Sticky Late Cycle AI at 34.1%, and AI earnings resilience is still a named bullish driver. This priority therefore focuses on quality ex-AI broadening beneficiaries rather than duplicating the existing small-cap priority or chasing high-beta cyclicals. Edge should decay over weeks because the thesis is tied to leadership rotation, breadth confirmation/falsification, and near-term macro catalysts: May CPI on 2026-06-11 and the June FOMC on 2026-06-17, where the stale Fed path still showed 70% hold and roughly 80% hold/hike odds.
research_priority.edge_hypothesis: The market may be mispricing broadening as either an AI-continuation trade or a generic small-cap/high-beta catch-up trade. The regime data points to a narrower opportunity: profitable ex-AI large- and mid-cap companies with durable free cash flow, improving relative breadth, and limited balance-sheet sensitivity. Consensus appears still anchored to cap-weight AI leadership because RSP continues to lag SPY and AI earnings resilience remains a major regime driver, while the improving ADL, high percent-above-200D, and small-cap relative strength indicate participation is broadening underneath the index. The mispricing is that quality ex-AI beneficiaries of broad participation are not being credited for soft-landing breadth improvement, while lower-quality beta may already be too vulnerable to the still-restrictive Fed path.
sub_questions: Which ex-AI sectors and industries have outperformed the S&P 500 equal-weight index over the last 4-8 weeks while also showing positive earnings-revision breadth?
Which profitable large- and mid-cap ex-AI companies combine positive free-cash-flow yield, net debt/EBITDA below sector median, and improving relative strength versus SPY?
Is recent broadening being led by quality factors or by lower-quality/high-beta short-covering, as measured by factor returns, balance-sheet quality, and short-interest changes?
Which non-AI cyclicals have the strongest sensitivity to tight credit spreads but the least sensitivity to a renewed rise in Fed hold/hike probabilities?
Where do ETF flows and active-fund holdings show under-ownership of ex-AI quality cash-flow beneficiaries relative to their improving price and revision trends?

regime.environment: Late-cycle tightening with narrow AI leadership
regime.regime_label: Reopening / Soft Landing narrowly leads a contested tape; sticky AI leadership remains a near-equal runner-up. Top macro-supported themes are Grid and power infrastructure, Quality ex-AI cash flow, Cash and short duration.
regime.headline: Forecast narrowly favors broadening soft-landing participation over sticky late-cycle AI leadership, but the two are effectively a coin-flip.
regime.summary: The model assigns the highest probability to Reopening / Soft Landing at 36.2%; runner-up sticky_late_cycle_ai at 34.1%. The gap is only ~2 points, so leadership direction is genuinely contested rather than resolved. The largest displayed deterministic driver is weak equal-weight-vs-cap-weight breadth (-0.30), which cuts against broadening, while resilient AI earnings (+0.52 into sticky AI) and healthy credit keep narrow leadership viable. Reported scenario probabilities are historically calibrated after the deterministic update; note that calibration narrowed a large deterministic soft-landing lead (47%) down to a near-tie, so the blended call rests heavily on the analogue layer. Dominant scenario: Reopening / Soft Landing (36%); runner-up scenario: Sticky Late Cycle AI (34%). Probability mode: historically_calibrated. Key macro tension: breadth signals conflict - cap-weight concentration says narrow, but advance-decline, percent-above-200D, and small-cap leadership say participation is improving.
regime.risk_summary: Credit is healthy and volatility is orderly, which keeps the regime from becoming fully risk-off. The decisive question is breadth: equal-weight still lags cap-weight, but ADL slope, percent-above-200D, and IWM-over-SPY leadership are improving - a broadening confirmation would tip the balance toward soft landing, while renewed narrowing would restore sticky AI. Fed path remains restrictive (hold/hike ~80%, though that read is dated 05/19 and should be refreshed). Historical analogues disagree with the deterministic engine on downside: analogues map materially more weight to Late Cycle Risk-Off than the rule-based layer does, so the risk-off tail is likely understated by the blended 12%. Tail probabilities remain visible: risk-off 12%, oil inflation tail 10%, AI capex rollover 7% (floored).
